# Getting started

The `orbit` command deploys a folder of static files to your account. This page walks through installing it, logging in
and publishing a first site. It takes about ten minutes on a normal connection.

<Callout kind="note">
  You need Node.js 20 or later. Run `node --version` to check which version you have.
</Callout>

## Install

```bash
npm install --global @orbit/cli
# TODO: remove the beta tag once 2.0 ships
orbit --version
```

## Log in

Run `orbit login`. The CLI opens your browser; approve the request and return to the terminal. Your token is stored in
the system keychain, so you do not have to log in again on this machine.

## Deploy a folder

<Steps>
  <li>Build your site, for example with `npm run build`.</li>
  <li>Run `orbit deploy ./dist` from the project folder.</li>
  <li>Open the address the CLI prints at the end.</li>
</Steps>

## Custom domains

Point a CNAME record at `sites.orbit.dev`. Certificates are issued automatically once the record resolves. Domain
changes take effect when DNS propagates, usually within an hour. If they do not, check the record with `dig`.

| Plan | Sites | Bandwidth per month | Build minutes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Hobby | 3 | 100 GB | 300 |
| Team | 50+ | 1 TB | 3,000 |
| Business | 500+ | 10 TB | 25,000 |

The limits above apply per account. A site that exceeds them is paused, not deleted, and resumes when the next billing
period starts. Keyboard focus moves to the first error when a deploy fails, and the progress bar shows each upload.
